headline: They Finally Started Brian Robinson. He Scored 4.04.
kicker: (week 5: 5.66, 7.70, 13.16, 25.20 on the bench, 4.04 in the lineup)
lede: For four weeks Brian Robinson improved on Barrett's bench: 5.66, 7.70, 13.16, 25.20. This week Barrett finally started him. He scored 4.04. Barrett also started Oronde Gadsden at flex, a free agent picked up at 1:34 on Sunday afternoon, who scored 0.00, the second straight week a Barrett flex has scored nothing. He went 2-0 anyway and is 9-1, because Barrett always gets away with it. The median hit 138.60, the highest line of the season for the second week running. Tom cleared it by 42 cents and Will, the man he was playing, missed it by 42 cents. Will paid $15 for Matthew Stafford at 3:19 on Sunday morning, benched him, and lost by 0.84 while Stafford threw for 383 yards. Anuj won his first game of the season, against a number. Greg (Miley) played a perfect lineup because his entire bench was on bye. Leo the Cleo is 10-0.

sections.awards: Fourteen citations, one per team. Leo the Cleo's is a formality.
sections.power: Season to date: record, points, all-play and this week's form, weighted, with movement from last week. Best lineup is the record each team would own if it had started its best legal lineup every week, everyone else exactly as they played. The tax is the difference: wins left on your own bench.
sections.median: Week 5's line was 138.60, the highest of the season for the second straight week. Tom made it by 0.42. Will, his opponent, missed it by 0.42. Anuj lost his game and won his first game of the year here; Maclane won his game and lost here by 25.22. Right of the line is a win.
sections.standings: Week 5 scoring, both results, and how much of your own roster you managed to start. Efficiency is what you scored over what your best legal lineup would have scored. Injured reserve does not count against you. Neither, it turns out, does a bench full of byes.
sections.bench: 129.24 points of lineup regret this week, down from 192.64. The cleanest week of the season, and it still included a 383-yard quarterback on a bench.
sections.faab: Every dollar of Week 5, audited. Maclane spent $66 of it in one run. Will spent $15 on a quarterback to bench. Greg (IR) made six adds. This is a receipt, not a shopping list.
sections.money: Auction dollars against everything each player has scored so far, started or not. A.J. Brown: $45, 4.1 points, still $10.98 a point.
sections.studs: The best and worst starts of Week 5, measured against what Yahoo thought they would do. CeeDee Lamb cost $52 and caught two balls for nine yards.
sections.games: The long version, closest game first.

awards.title: Bench Graduate

awards.title: Forty-Two Cents

awards.line: Last week he beat every team but one. This week he beat nobody. Started Roman Wilson for 0.00 a week after benching his 15.9, and paid $8 for Adonai Mitchell to score zero for a second franchise.

awards.line: Lost to the undefeated team by 10.62, beat the median by 7.76. A win is a win. The first one took five weeks.

awards.title: Five Touchdowns, Zero Wins

awards.title: Darnold Over Nix, The Sequel
awards.line: Benched the $20 quarterback for Bo Nix again. Darnold outscored him again, by 2.38. Best lineup wins by 10.62. Lost by 7.86.

awards.title: Snapped It
awards.line: Three straight 0-2 weeks, then a 2-0 by 37.20. Isaiah Likely, 26.9. Carnell Tate, 8.8 on the bench in Week 3, started this week for 1.1.

awards.title: Ten And Oh
awards.line: 13-0 in all-play, the high score, $0 spent this week. Same award as last week, two more wins.

awards.title: Best Bench Decision Of The Week
awards.line: Kenyon Sadiq, $18: 0.00 as a starter in Week 4, -0.70 on the bench in Week 5. Nathan learns. Slowly, and only about tight ends.

games.note: Will paid $15 for Matthew Stafford on waivers, processed at 3:19 on Sunday morning, then benched him for Joe Burrow. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns, 27.32 points, on the bench. Burrow scored 24.60. In Week 3 Greg (Miley) benched Stafford's 390 yards. Two managers, two benchings, 773 yards nobody started. The quarterback was not even the worst of it: Denzel Boston caught a touchdown for 12.62 on the bench and Terry McLaurin scored 10.2 there, while KC Concepcion (1.0) and Romeo Doubs (2.1) started. Boston for Concepcion alone wins this game. Will's best lineup scores 160.62 and wins by 21.60. Stafford for Burrow alone wins it. Instead he lost by 0.84, missed the median by 0.42 and went 0-2. Tom paid $9 for Jacoby Brissett with Patrick Mahomes on bye, got 25.78, cleared the median by 0.42 and is 9-1. Tom's waiver receipts this season: $7 for Emanuel Wilson, $9 for Brissett, both started, both paid.

Maclane spent $66 of FAAB in one waiver run on Wednesday morning: $41 on Keon Coleman, $21 on Dohnte Meyers and $4 on Aaron Rodgers. The $4 quarterback threw three touchdowns for 22.00. The $41 receiver scored 7.2. The $21 receiver sat on the bench and scored 7.36. Maclane has $16 left. He scored 113.38, the fourth-lowest score of the week, missed the median by 25.22, and still won his game, because he drew Jon. Jon started Bo Nix (7.92) over Sam Darnold (10.30) for the second straight week, the $20 quarterback he bought to bench. Kendrick Bourne, a Wednesday free agent, scored 9.5 on the bench and Rashod Bateman 8.7, while David Montgomery ($23) scored 1.1 and Brian Thomas Jr. scored 1.0, all of it from one solo tackle. T.J. Watt scored zero. Jon's best lineup scores 124.00 and wins by 10.62. Jaylen Warren scored 34.8 and it was nowhere near enough.

Four weeks of Brian Robinson on the bench: 5.66, 7.70, 13.16, 25.20. Week 5, Barrett finally started him: 4.04, on sixteen rushing yards. The bench was the only thing holding him together. Barrett also picked up Oronde Gadsden on Sunday afternoon and started him at flex for 0.00, the second week in a row a Barrett flex has scored zero (Ladd McConkey, who did it last week, scored 0.00 again from the bench). Kendre Miller scored 9.0 on the bench. Barrett won by 8.10 and cleared the median by 0.92, after clearing it by 0.26 and then 0.56. He is 9-1 and nobody can explain it. Nishil got 39.46 out of Drake Maye, the best start of the week, and lost both games anyway. He started the Commanders, a Wednesday free agent, for 9.86 while the Seahawks scored 14.52 on his bench. He paid $21 for Will Shipley (7.8). Chase Brown ($44) scored 5.5. Nishil is 1-9 and 0-5 against the median.

Chris is 10-0, went 13-0 in all-play and posted the high score of the week, 156.98. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 37.2 and Josh Allen ran for 121 yards. Chris has spent $5 of FAAB all season and claimed two more players this week for $0. Anuj scored 146.36, the fourth-highest score of the week, went 10-3 in all-play, and lost to the one team that mattered. He still won his first game of the season, against the median, by 7.76. Puka Nacua caught 17 balls. Anuj also picked up Jauan Jennings at 12:06 on Sunday and started him at flex: 0.00. His best lineup scores 149.76 and still loses. 1-9. The milk has turned into something that resembles a team, a week too late to matter against this opponent.

Andrew started the right quarterback for the second week running: Dak Prescott 14.64, Jalen Hurts 13.00 on the bench. This time it paid. Bucky Irving scored 32.5, Christian Watson 30.3, and Andrew went 2-0 for the first time since Week 3. He found new places to hide points instead: J.K. Dobbins 14.4 and Kyle Pitts 12.7 on the bench, Jeremiyah Love 2.2 at flex and Harold Fannin 0.9 at tight end. 24.00 points of regret, the most in the league, in a 12.52-point win. Darrius missed the median by 0.58 and went 0-2. His best lineup clears it: Keenan Allen's 7.0 on the bench for DK Metcalf's 3.8, Jaylen Wright's 3.22 for RJ Harvey's 0.7. Darrius has scored 691.40 points, the second most in the league, and is 4-6. His best-lineup record is 8-2. He has the worst luck in the league, and this week he helped it.

Greg (Miley) played a perfect lineup: 100.0 percent efficiency, every call correct. That is because his entire bench was on bye. Tetairoa McMillan, Rashee Rice, Brycen Tremayne, Bryce Young and Jalen Coker scored zero between them and could not have been started if he tried. He even started the right quarterback, Jared Goff 28.94, because Bryce Young was not playing. Remove Greg's choices and he gets every one right. He scored 108.10 and lost by 37.20. Abhishek snapped a run of three straight 0-2 weeks behind Isaiah Likely, 11 catches and two touchdowns for 26.9, and Mike Evans' 23.8. He still found a way: Carnell Tate, 8.8 on his bench in Week 3, started at flex this week and scored 1.1, with Josh Cameron's 7.52 on the bench. Dameon Pierce, a Saturday free agent, started and scored 3.16.

The biggest margin of the week. Jayden Daniels ran for two touchdowns and 33.26 and Nathan played a 99.3 percent lineup, with CeeDee Lamb's 1.9 the only stain. Kenyon Sadiq, the $18 tight end who scored 0.00 as a starter last week, scored -0.70 on the bench this week. Benching him was the best call Nathan made. 9-1, 5-0 head to head, $7 of FAAB, none of it spent. Greg (IR) went from 12-1 in all-play last week to 0-13 this week, the league low at 104.30. He started Roman Wilson, the receiver whose 15.9 on the bench cost him last week, and Roman Wilson scored 0.00. He paid $8 for Blake Corum and benched him for 14.7. He paid another $8 for Adonai Mitchell, the player Jon started in Week 3 for exactly zero, and Mitchell scored zero again. Greg is on 32 moves. His best lineup scores 122.90 and still goes 0-2.
